name: Deadlight — Shelf Guerrilla Mural Collective
description: Deadlight operates in the deep Tier 1 Shelf, creating massive unauthorized murals on the underside of elevated infrastructure — support pylons, overpass ceilings, drainage channel walls — surfaces that require technical climbing skill to reach and that corporate clean crews rarely bother with. Their work is site-specific and impermanent by design, using paint formulations that change color with temperature and humidity, so the murals are never the same twice. Deadlight's founding trio — Xochitl Ferreira-Obi, Smoke (unidentified), and a synthetic called Pale Mirror — established the rule that no piece can be signed with a name, only a small dead-light symbol: a circle with a crossed-out interior.
cultural_impact: Deadlight murals have become informal landmarks and navigation points in Shelf communities where official signage is absent or vandalized — residents give directions by Deadlight pieces. Several pieces have been documented and sold as NFT-equivalent 'moment captures' by third parties without the collective's consent, a practice they actively sabotage.
locations: The Underpass Gallery (unofficial, rotating sites under I-94 remnant)
story_hooks: Smoke's identity has been discovered by a corporate investigator hired by a developer who wants to demolish a Deadlight site — the collective must decide whether to protect Smoke or go public first.
Pale Mirror is experiencing memory fragmentation and their contribution to recent pieces has become increasingly erratic and disturbing — the collective doesn't know if it's art or distress.

A city infrastructure project will destroy twelve Deadlight sites simultaneously — preservation advocates want to document them, but Deadlight's founding principle is that the work should die with its surface.
